2.07.6 — Immutable executed artifact

When execution completes, create the repository record in the same logical process.

async def register_executed_agreement(
    db,
    agreement,
    execution_package,
    executed_document,
):

    if agreement.status != "EXECUTED":
        raise ValueError(
            "Agreement is not executed."
        )

    executed_document.immutable = True

    record = AgreementRepositoryRecord(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        executed_document_id=executed_document.id,
        execution_package_id=execution_package.id,
        record_status="ACTIVE",
        effective_at=agreement.effective_at,
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(record)

    await create_audit_event(
        db=db,
        actor=None,
        action="EXECUTED_AGREEMENT_REGISTERED",
        entity_id=agreement.id,
    )

    return record
2.07.7 — Prevent document mutation

Do not rely only on the frontend.

At service level:

async def update_document(
    db,
    document_id,
    changes,
):

    document = await get_document(
        db,
        document_id,
    )

    if document.immutable:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail=(
                "Immutable legal document cannot "
                "be modified."
            ),
        )

    apply_changes(
        document,
        changes,
    )

Better still, enforce critical invariants using database permissions/triggers for immutable legal records.

2.07.8 — Secure storage

The actual file should never live directly in PostgreSQL.

Use private object storage:

S3-compatible storage
        ↓
private bucket
        ↓
encrypted object

Storage key:

tenants/{organization_id}/
agreements/{agreement_id}/
documents/{document_id}/
artifact

Never construct storage paths using unsanitized filenames.

Use generated IDs.

2.07.9 — Upload pipeline

All uploaded documents should follow:

Upload
 ↓
Size/type validation
 ↓
Virus/malware scanning
 ↓
Content validation
 ↓
Hash calculation
 ↓
Private object storage
 ↓
Database registration
 ↓
Audit event

Example:

async def ingest_document(
    *,
    db,
    organization_id,
    agreement_id,
    upload,
    document_type_id,
    actor_id,
):

    raw = await upload.read()

    validate_size(raw)
    validate_declared_media_type(upload.content_type)
    validate_file_signature(raw)

    scan_result = await malware_scanner.scan(raw)

    if not scan_result.clean:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail="Document failed security scanning.",
        )

    digest = sha256(raw)

    document_id = uuid.uuid4()

    storage_key = build_storage_key(
        organization_id=organization_id,
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        document_id=document_id,
    )

    await object_storage.put_private(
        key=storage_key,
        data=raw,
        content_type=upload.content_type,
    )

    document = Document(
        id=document_id,
        organization_id=organization_id,
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        document_type_id=document_type_id,
        title=secure_filename(upload.filename),
        filename=secure_filename(upload.filename),
        media_type=upload.content_type,
        storage_key=storage_key,
        sha256=digest,
        size_bytes=len(raw),
        classification=DocumentClassification.SUPPORTING_DOCUMENT,
        status=DocumentStatus.ACTIVE,
        immutable=False,
        created_by=actor_id,
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(document)

    await db.flush()

    await create_audit_event(
        db=db,
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="DOCUMENT_INGESTED",
        entity_id=document.id,
    )

    return document
2.07.10 — Hashing
import hashlib


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

For large documents, avoid loading everything into memory in production.

Use streaming hashing:

def hash_stream(stream):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()

    while True:
        chunk = stream.read(1024 * 1024)

        if not chunk:
            break

        digest.update(chunk)

    return digest.hexdigest()
2.07.11 — Secure download

Users should never receive direct bucket access.

@router.get(
    "/agreements/{agreement_id}/documents/{document_id}/download"
)
async def download_document(
    agreement_id: UUID,
    document_id: UUID,
    current_user=Depends(get_current_user),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
):

    document = await get_authorized_agreement_document(
        db=db,
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        document_id=document_id,
        user=current_user,
    )

    verify_document_access(
        current_user,
        document,
    )

    verify_object_exists(
        document.storage_key
    )

    url = await object_storage.create_presigned_url(
        document.storage_key,
        expires_seconds=300,
    )

    await create_audit_event(
        db=db,
        actor_id=current_user.id,
        action="DOCUMENT_ACCESSED",
        entity_id=document.id,
    )

    await db.commit()

    return {
        "url": url,
        "expires_in": 300,
        "sha256": document.sha256,
    }

2.07.17 — Executed-document verification

Add:

GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/verify

Response:

{
  "document_id": "actual-id",
  "stored_sha256": "actual-hash",
  "calculated_sha256": "calculated-hash",
  "match": true,
  "immutable": true,
  "status": "ACTIVE"
}

The verification service should calculate against the stored object rather than simply trusting the database hash.

async def verify_document_integrity(
    document,
):

    content = await object_storage.get(
        document.storage_key
    )

    calculated = sha256(content)

    return {
        "stored_sha256": document.sha256,
        "calculated_sha256": calculated,
        "match": calculated == document.sha256,
        "immutable": document.immutable,
    }

For large files this should become an asynchronous verification job.

2.07.19 — Evidence generation
async def generate_evidence_package(
    db,
    agreement_id,
    actor_id,
):

    require_agreement_access(
        db,
        agreement_id,
        actor_id,
    )

        db,

        db,

2.07.21 — Retention calculation
async def calculate_retention(
    db,
    document,
):

    policy = await resolve_retention_policy(
        db,
        document,
    )

    if not policy:
        return None

    trigger_date = await resolve_trigger_date(
        db,
        document,
        policy.trigger_event,
    )

    if not trigger_date:
        return None

    return trigger_date + timedelta(
        days=policy.duration_days
    )

The system should store the calculated date and the rule version used to calculate it.

2.07.22 — Legal hold

2.07.23 — Disposal protection
async def can_dispose_document(
    db,
    document,
):

    if document.immutable:
        return False, "Immutable legal record."

    holds = await active_legal_holds_for_document(
        db,
        document.id,
    )

    if holds:
        return False, "Document is under legal hold."

    retention = await get_retention_state(
        db,
        document.id,
    )

    if retention and not retention.expired:
        return False, "Retention period has not expired."

    return True, None

Even after retention expiry, disposal should normally be an explicit controlled process rather than an automatic destructive action.

2.07.24 — Archive versus delete

Use:

ACTIVE
   ↓
ARCHIVED
   ↓
DISPOSITION_ELIGIBLE
   ↓
DISPOSED

Not:

ACTIVE → DELETE

And for immutable executed agreements:

EXECUTED
   ↓
ACTIVE
   ↓
ARCHIVED

The legal record remains represented even when physical storage lifecycle rules eventually change.

2.07.26 — Consolidated agreement view

Users still need to understand:

“What are the terms currently in force?”

So create a derived consolidated view.

Original agreement
      +
effective amendments
      +
effective change orders
      ↓
CURRENT CONSOLIDATED TERMS

But:

The consolidated view is an interpretation/derived representation. It does not replace the underlying legally executed documents.

This distinction is crucial.

2.07.27 — Consolidation service
async def build_consolidated_terms(
    db,
    agreement_id,
):

    base = await get_original_executed_terms(
        db,
        agreement_id,
    )

    amendments = await get_effective_amendments(
        db,
        agreement_id,
    )

    state = base

    for amendment in amendments:
        state = apply_amendment(
            state,
            amendment,
        )

    return state

The function should use the structured clause/version representation from the earlier milestones, not arbitrary string replacement.

2.07.36 — API authorization dependency
async def require_document_access(
    document_id,
    current_user,
    db,
):

    document = await get_document(
        db,
        document_id,
    )

    if not document:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
        )

    allowed = await authorization_service.can_view_document(
        user=current_user,
        document=document,
    )

    if not allowed:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
        )

    return document

Return 404 where appropriate to avoid leaking the existence of protected records.

2.07.37 — Retention worker

Use Celery.

@celery_app.task
def evaluate_retention_records():

    async_run(
        retention_service.evaluate_all_due_records()
    )

The service:

async def evaluate_all_due_records():

    records = await find_due_records()

    for record in records:

        if await has_active_legal_hold(
            record.document_id
        ):
            continue

        await mark_disposition_eligible(
            record
        )

        await create_audit_event(
            action="RETENTION_ELIGIBLE",
            entity_id=record.document_id,
        )

Do not automatically destroy legal records merely because the timer fired.

2.07.38 — Legal-hold worker

Legal holds must prevent disposition immediately.

async def place_legal_hold(
    db,
    hold,
    document_ids,
    actor_id,
):

    verify_can_manage_legal_holds(
        actor_id
    )

    for document_id in document_ids:

        await attach_document_to_hold(
            db,
            hold.id,
            document_id,
        )

        document = await get_document(
            db,
            document_id,
        )

        document.status = (
            DocumentStatus.UNDER_LEGAL_HOLD
        )

    await create_audit_event(
        db=db,
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="LEGAL_HOLD_PLACED",
        entity_id=hold.id,
    )

    await db.commit()

2.07.44 — One important architectural correction

There is one thing I would lock down now before continuing further.

Do not make this:

Agreement
 └── latest_document.pdf

Make it:

Agreement
│
├── Draft versions
├── Negotiation versions
├── Final negotiated version
│
├── Execution package
│   ├── execution requirements
│   ├── signer definitions
│   ├── signing order
│   └── execution evidence
│
├── Executed artifacts
│
├── Amendments
│   ├── amendment versions
│   └── amendment execution artifacts
│
├── Supporting documents
│
├── Obligations / evidence
│
├── Termination documents
│
└── Retention / legal hold records

That structure prevents a huge class of future problems around document provenance, audits, amendments, and legal evidence.

2.08 — Obligations & Contract Operations Workspace

This milestone makes the platform operational after execution.

Until now:

Agreement
   ↓
Negotiate
   ↓
Approve
   ↓
Sign
   ↓
Execute
   ↓
Store

Now:

Executed Agreement
        ↓
Contractual Obligations
        ↓
Responsible Party / Owner
        ↓
Deadline Calculation
        ↓
Reminders
        ↓
Evidence
        ↓
Review
        ↓
Compliance State
        ↓
Escalation
        ↓
Renewal / Amendment / Termination Impact

The core principle is:

An obligation must be traceable to an actual contractual source, actual party, actual date/rule, and actual evidence.

No invented deadlines. No fake owners. No synthetic completion percentages.

2.08.2 — Obligation lifecycle

Use a state machine.

CANDIDATE
   ↓
CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED
   ↓
CONFIRMED
   ↓
ASSIGNED
   ↓
OPEN
   ↓
IN_PROGRESS
   ↓
COMPLETED

Alternative branches:

OPEN
 ├── OVERDUE
 ├── WAIVED
 ├── CANCELLED
 └── SUPERSEDED

And for verification:

COMPLETED
    ↓
EVIDENCE_SUBMITTED
    ↓
UNDER_REVIEW
    ↓
VERIFIED

Do not treat:

completed = verified

because someone can claim completion without acceptable evidence.

2.08.3 — Obligation model
# backend/app/obligations/models.py

class ObligationStatus(str, enum.Enum):

2.08.4 — Why source_version_id matters

Suppose the original agreement says:

Payment due within 30 days.

Then Amendment #2 changes it to:

Payment due within 45 days.

The system must know:

Old obligation
      ↓
superseded

New obligation
      ↓
derived from Amendment #2

Therefore the source must remain traceable to the exact contract version.

2.08.7 — Absolute versus relative deadlines

Your engine must support both.

Absolute
Payment due:
2026-11-30
Relative
Payment due:
30 calendar days after invoice
Event-relative
Notice:
10 business days after breach notification
Recurring
Monthly reporting
Quarterly certification
Annual renewal

Represent the rule structurally.

{
  "type": "RELATIVE",
  "unit": "DAYS",
  "amount": 30,
  "calendar": "CALENDAR_DAYS",
  "reference": "INVOICE_DATE"
}

For a business-day calculation:

{
  "type": "RELATIVE",
  "unit": "DAYS",
  "amount": 10,
  "calendar": "BUSINESS_DAYS",
  "reference": "BREACH_NOTICE_DATE"
}

The system must derive these structures from actual contract content or explicit user configuration.

2.08.8 — Deadline calculator
# backend/app/obligations/deadlines.py

from datetime import datetime, timedelta


def calculate_absolute_deadline(
    date_value: datetime,
) -> datetime:

    return date_value


def calculate_relative_deadline(
    source_date: datetime,
    amount: int,
    unit: str,
) -> datetime:

    if unit == "DAYS":
        return source_date + timedelta(days=amount)

    if unit == "HOURS":
        return source_date + timedelta(hours=amount)

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported time unit: {unit}"
    )

For real business-day rules, create a calendar service instead of approximating Monday–Friday.

2.08.11 — Obligation extraction

There are now two sources.

Deterministic extraction

From structured agreement clauses.

Clause schema
   ↓
known obligation field
   ↓
obligation candidate
AI-assisted extraction

From unstructured agreement text.

document/version
      ↓
AI extraction
      ↓
candidate obligation
      ↓
exact evidence
      ↓
human confirmation
      ↓
confirmed obligation

AI must never silently convert a prediction into a binding obligation.

2.08.12 — AI extraction schema
class ObligationCandidate(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str

    source_document_id: UUID
    source_version_id: UUID

    source_text: str

    party_reference: str | None = None

    deadline_rule: dict | None = None

    criticality: str

    confidence: float

Then validate:

def validate_candidate(
    candidate: ObligationCandidate,
):
    if not candidate.source_text.strip():
        raise ValueError(
            "Source evidence is required."
        )

    if not 0 <= candidate.confidence <= 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "Confidence must be between 0 and 1."
        )
2.08.13 — Candidate creation
async def create_obligation_candidate(
    db,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    extracted_data,
    model_run_id=None,
):

    source = await verify_source_location(
        db,
        agreement_id,
        extracted_data.source_document_id,
        extracted_data.source_version_id,
    )

    candidate = Obligation(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=source.organization_id,
        source_document_id=source.document_id,
        source_version_id=source.version_id,
        source_text=extracted_data.source_text,
        title=extracted_data.title,
        description=extracted_data.description,
        criticality=map_criticality(
            extracted_data.criticality
        ),
        status=ObligationStatus.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED,
        metadata={
            "ai_model_run_id": str(model_run_id)
            if model_run_id
            else None,
            "confidence": extracted_data.confidence,
        },
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(candidate)

    return candidate

2.08.15 — Confirmation API
POST /api/v1/obligations/{id}/confirm
@router.post(
    "/{obligation_id}/confirm"
)
async def confirm_obligation(
    obligation_id: UUID,
    payload: ObligationConfirmationRequest,
    current_user=Depends(require_obligation_reviewer),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
):

    obligation = await get_authorized_obligation(
        db,
        obligation_id,
        current_user,
    )

    if obligation.status != (
        ObligationStatus.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED
    ):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail="Obligation is not awaiting confirmation.",
        )

    await verify_source_still_current(
        db,
        obligation,
    )

    obligation.status = ObligationStatus.CONFIRMED

    await create_audit_event(
        db,
        actor_id=current_user.id,
        action="OBLIGATION_CONFIRMED",
        entity_id=obligation.id,
    )

    await db.commit()

    return obligation
2.08.16 — Assigning ownership

Backend verifies both IDs against the same agreement.

async def validate_assignee(
    db,
    obligation,
    agreement_party_id,
    member_id,
):

    party = await get_agreement_party(
        db,
        agreement_party_id,
    )

    if party.agreement_id != obligation.agreement_id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Party does not belong to agreement.",
        )

    member = await get_agreement_member(
        db,
        member_id,
    )

    if member.agreement_id != obligation.agreement_id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Member does not belong to agreement.",
        )

2.08.18 — Evidence review
async def verify_obligation_evidence(
    db,
    evidence,
    reviewer,
):

    require_evidence_reviewer(
        reviewer,
        evidence,
    )

    document = await get_document(
        db,
        evidence.document_id,
    )

    integrity = await verify_document_integrity(
        document
    )

    if not integrity["match"]:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail="Evidence document integrity check failed.",
        )

    evidence.status = EvidenceStatus.VERIFIED
    evidence.reviewed_by = reviewer.id
    evidence.reviewed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    obligation = await get_obligation(
        db,
        evidence.obligation_id,
    )

    obligation.evidence_status = (
        EvidenceStatus.VERIFIED
    )

    if obligation.status in {
        ObligationStatus.IN_PROGRESS,
        ObligationStatus.OPEN,
    }:
        obligation.status = (
            ObligationStatus.COMPLETED
        )

async def evaluate():

    obligations = await find_open_obligations_needing_reminder()

    for obligation in obligations:

        recipients = await resolve_obligation_recipients(
            obligation
        )

        for recipient in recipients:

            await create_notification(
                recipient=recipient,
                type="OBLIGATION_REMINDER",
                entity_id=obligation.id,

Actual notification delivery then goes through your existing outbox/notification engine.

2.08.22 — Overdue detection

The system should calculate overdue state dynamically or update it through a controlled scheduler.

async def evaluate_overdue_state(
    obligation,
    now,
):

    deadline = await get_current_deadline(
        obligation.id
    )

    if not deadline:
        return

    if (
        deadline.due_at < now
        and obligation.status in {
            ObligationStatus.OPEN,
            ObligationStatus.IN_PROGRESS,
        }
    ):
        obligation.status = (
            ObligationStatus.OVERDUE
        )

2.08.24 — Escalation service
async def evaluate_escalations(
    db,
    obligation,
):

    rules = await get_matching_rules(
        db,
        obligation.organization_id,
    )

    for rule in rules:

        if rule_matches(
            obligation,
            rule,
        ):

            recipients = await resolve_rule_recipients(
                db,
                obligation,
                rule,
            )

            for recipient in recipients:

                await emit_escalation(
                    db,
                    obligation,
                    recipient,
                    rule,
                )

Use idempotency so the same overdue event does not generate unlimited notifications.

2.08.29 — Status transition service

Do not allow arbitrary API clients to write:

{
  "status": "COMPLETED"
}

Instead:

ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS = {
    "CANDIDATE": {"CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED"},
    "CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED": {
        "CONFIRMED",
        "CANCELLED",
    },
    "CONFIRMED": {"ASSIGNED"},
    "ASSIGNED": {"OPEN"},
    "OPEN": {
        "IN_PROGRESS",
        "COMPLETED",
        "WAIVED",
        "CANCELLED",
    },
    "IN_PROGRESS": {
        "COMPLETED",
        "WAIVED",
        "CANCELLED",
    },
    "OVERDUE": {
        "IN_PROGRESS",
        "COMPLETED",
        "WAIVED",
    },
}

Then:

def ensure_valid_transition(
    current,
    target,
):

    allowed = ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(
        current,
        set(),
    )

    if target not in allowed:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid transition {current} -> {target}"
        )

For production, move the state transition definition into your workflow/configuration model where practical so organization-specific workflows do not require code changes.

2.08.30 — Complete obligation operation
async def complete_obligation(
    db,
    obligation,
    actor,
):

    require_can_complete(
        actor,
        obligation,
    )

    if obligation.evidence_status == (
        EvidenceStatus.REQUIRED
    ):
        evidence = await get_valid_evidence(
            db,
            obligation.id,
        )

        if not evidence:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=422,
                detail=(
                    "Required evidence has not "
                    "been submitted."
                ),
            )

    ensure_valid_transition(
        obligation.status.value,
        "COMPLETED",
    )

    previous = obligation.status.value

    obligation.status = (
        ObligationStatus.COMPLETED
    )
    obligation.updated_at = (
        datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    )

    db.add(
        ObligationEvent(
            obligation_id=obligation.id,
            event_type="COMPLETED",
            actor_id=actor.id,
            previous_status=previous,
            new_status="COMPLETED",
            metadata={},
            created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )
    )

    await create_audit_event(
        db,
        actor_id=actor.id,
        action="OBLIGATION_COMPLETED",
        entity_id=obligation.id,
    )

    await db.commit()
2.08.31 — Amendment propagation

This is where 1.18 becomes operational.

Suppose:

Original:
Report due 15th every month.

Amendment #2:
Report due 20th every month.

When Amendment #2 becomes effective:

Old obligation
    ↓
SUPERSEDED

New obligation/rule
    ↓
OPEN

Never silently modify the old obligation's provenance.

async def apply_amendment_to_obligations(
    db,
    amendment,
):

    affected = await find_affected_obligations(
        db,
        amendment,
    )

    for obligation in affected:

        if amendment_changes_obligation(
            amendment,
            obligation,
        ):

            obligation.status = (
                ObligationStatus.SUPERSEDED
            )

            replacement = await create_replacement_obligation(
                db,
                source_amendment=amendment,
                previous_obligation=obligation,
            )

            await link_obligation_versions(
                db,
                previous=obligation,
                replacement=replacement,
            )

2.08.38 — Cross-contract conflict detection

A useful deterministic engine:

async def detect_deadline_conflicts(
    obligations,
):

    conflicts = []

    for left in obligations:
        for right in obligations:

            if left.id == right.id:
                continue

            if same_assignee(left, right) and dates_overlap(
                left,
                right,
            ):
                conflicts.append(
                    build_conflict(
                        left,
                        right,
                    )
                )

    return conflicts

For scale, replace the O(n²) implementation with interval queries or PostgreSQL range types.

2.08.41 — Dashboard query

Do not run dozens of independent queries for every dashboard card.

Create a service-level aggregate query.

async def get_operations_dashboard(
    db,
    organization_id,
    member_id,
):

    return {
        "open": await count_open(
            db,
            organization_id,
        ),
        "due_soon": await count_due_soon(
            db,
            organization_id,
            member_id,
        ),
        "overdue": await count_overdue(
            db,
            organization_id,
        ),
        "pending_evidence": await count_pending_evidence(
            db,
            organization_id,
        ),
        "my_obligations": await count_assigned(
            db,
            member_id,
        ),
    }

Later optimize with materialized views when actual scale justifies it.

2.08.42 — Authorization

Every operation must check:

organization
  ↓
agreement
  ↓
obligation
  ↓
assignee/role
  ↓
requested operation

Examples:

View obligation
→ agreement access

Confirm extracted obligation
→ legal reviewer / authorized role

Assign owner
→ agreement administrator / authorized role

Complete obligation
→ assigned performer or authorized role

Verify evidence
→ reviewer role

Create legal hold
→ authorized legal/admin role

Do not make:

if user.is_admin:
    allow_everything()

your only model.

2.08.43 — Security boundary

An employee may have:

organization access

but not:

agreement access

A lawyer may have:

agreement access

but not:

private counterparty notes

A party may have:

obligation visibility

but not:

internal legal review metadata

All of those distinctions already established in 1.11 must continue here.

2.09 — Contract Risk, Compliance & Exception Management

This milestone sits above the agreement, negotiation, repository, obligation, lifecycle, and AI layers.

The goal is not simply to produce a “risk score.”

The platform should answer:

What is wrong or potentially risky, exactly where is the evidence, why does it matter, who owns it, what action is required, and has the issue actually been resolved?

Architecture:

Agreement
   │
   ├── Contract clauses
   ├── Parties
   ├── Amendments
   ├── Obligations
   ├── Execution evidence
   ├── Lifecycle events
   └── External compliance data
           ↓
     Risk / Compliance Engine
           │
     ┌─────┴─────────┐
     ↓               ↓
Deterministic      AI-assisted
Rules              Findings
     ↓               ↓
     └──────┬────────┘
            ↓
      Evidence validation
            ↓
       Risk finding
            ↓
       Owner / remediation
            ↓
      Review / approval
            ↓
       Resolved / accepted

The distinction is critical:

AI finding ≠ legal fact
Risk score ≠ legal conclusion
Rule match ≠ breach
Potential issue ≠ confirmed violation

2.09.5 — Deterministic rules engine

This should execute before AI.

For example, a rule can detect:

required clause absent

or:

liability cap absent

or:

agreement expiration exists but renewal notice has no operational reminder

or:

required signer evidence absent

The rule engine operates on structured contract data.

2.09.7 — Rule execution

Do not write hundreds of:

if agreement.type == ...

statements into routes.

Use a rule engine.

class RuleEngine:

    async def evaluate(
        self,
        agreement,
        context,
    ):

        rules = await load_active_rules(
            context.db,
            agreement.organization_id,
        )

        findings = []

        for rule in rules:

            result = evaluate_rule(
                rule=rule,
                agreement=agreement,
                context=context,
            )

            if result.matched:
                findings.append(
                    build_finding(
                        rule,
                        result,
                    )
                )

        return findings
2.09.8 — Rule result
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class RuleResult:
    matched: bool
    severity: str | None
    evidence: list[dict]
    explanation: str | None
    metadata: dict

The engine should refuse to create a finding without enough evidence.

if result.matched and not result.evidence:
    raise ValueError(
        "A material rule finding requires evidence."
    )
2.09.9 — AI findings

AI should operate as a separate detector.

Agreement
   ↓
relevant source text
   ↓
AI analysis
   ↓
structured candidate
   ↓
schema validation
   ↓
source verification
   ↓
finding

Example model output:

    title: str
    explanation: str

    source_document_id: UUID
    source_version_id: UUID

        "MEDIUM",
        "HIGH",

2.09.10 — Verify AI evidence

Do not trust the AI's quoted text.

The server should independently find the referenced version/document and verify the excerpt.

async def verify_ai_evidence(
    db,
    candidate,
):

    source = await load_exact_source(
        db,
        document_id=candidate.source_document_id,
        version_id=candidate.source_version_id,
    )

    if not source:
        raise ValueError(
            "Referenced source does not exist."
        )

    if not source_contains_excerpt(
        source.text,
        candidate.source_excerpt,
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "AI evidence could not be verified."
        )

    return True

This dramatically reduces unsupported findings.

2.09.11 — Confidence is not severity

Keep these separate:

confidence
    =
how confident is the detector?

severity
    =
how material could the issue be?

For example:

95% confidence
MEDIUM severity

is perfectly valid.

And:

63% confidence
CRITICAL severity

might still require immediate human review.

Do not automatically calculate:

severity = confidence
2.09.12 — Risk scoring

Use a transparent scoring system.

A basic model:

risk_score =
probability × impact × exposure

Example implementation:

def calculate_risk_score(
    probability: float,
    impact: float,
    exposure: float,
) -> float:

    values = (
        probability,
        impact,
        exposure,
    )

    if not all(0 <= x <= 1 for x in values):
        raise ValueError(
            "Risk dimensions must be between 0 and 1."
        )

    return probability * impact * exposure

But don't expose a meaningless single number without its inputs.

Return:

{
  "score": 0.72,
  "probability": 0.80,
  "impact": 0.90,
  "exposure": 1.00
}

2.09.19 — Compliance evaluation
async def evaluate_compliance(
    db,
    agreement,
):

    policies = await load_applicable_policies(
        db,
        agreement,
    )

    results = []

    for policy in policies:

        result = evaluate_policy(
            policy=policy,
            agreement=agreement,
        )

        evaluation = await save_policy_evaluation(
            db=db,
            agreement=agreement,
            policy=policy,
            result=result,
        )

        results.append(evaluation)

    return results

    )

    result: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    evaluated_version_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
    )

    evidence: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
    )

    evaluated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

Possible results:

PASS
FAIL
REVIEW_REQUIRED
NOT_APPLICABLE
UNKNOWN

Use UNKNOWN rather than pretending the system knows something it cannot verify.

2.09.24 — Version awareness

Risk findings must be version-specific.

Imagine:

Version 5
    ↓
Finding: missing insurance clause

Version 6
    ↓
insurance clause added

The Version 5 finding should not simply disappear.

Instead:

Version 5 finding
    ↓
SUPERSEDED
    ↓
Version 6 evaluation
    ↓
RESOLVED / PASS

This gives you historical auditability.

2.09.37 — Risk service
async def analyze_agreement(
    db,
    agreement_id,
    version_id,
):

    agreement = await load_authorized_agreement(
        db,
        agreement_id,
    )

    version = await get_exact_version(
        db,
        agreement_id,
        version_id,
    )

    deterministic_findings = (
        await rule_engine.evaluate(
            agreement=agreement,
            context={
                "db": db,
                "version": version,
            },
        )
    )

    ai_findings = (
        await ai_risk_engine.analyze(
            agreement=agreement,
            version=version,
        )
    )

    verified_ai_findings = []

    for finding in ai_findings:
        if await verify_ai_evidence(
            db,
            finding,
        ):
            verified_ai_findings.append(
                finding
            )

    findings = (
        deterministic_findings
        + verified_ai_findings
    )

    await persist_findings(
        db,
        findings,
    )

    snapshot = await create_risk_snapshot(
        db,
        agreement,
        version,
        findings,
    )

    return snapshot
2.09.38 — Run analysis after real lifecycle events

Trigger evaluation after:

Agreement finalization
Execution
Amendment effective date
New supporting evidence
Relevant obligation failure
Policy change
External compliance update
Manual re-analysis

Use the existing outbox architecture.

Amendment executed
      ↓
Outbox
      ↓
Risk analysis job
      ↓
New snapshot
      ↓
Findings
      ↓
Notifications

Do not run expensive AI analysis directly inside the user's HTTP request.

2.09.39 — Celery task
@celery_app.task(
    autoretry_for=(Exception,),
    retry_backoff=True,
    max_retries=5,
)
def analyze_agreement_task(
    agreement_id,
    version_id,
):

    async_run(
        risk_service.analyze_agreement(
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            version_id=version_id,
        )
    )

Use idempotency keyed around:

agreement_id
version_id
analysis_configuration_version

so repeated events do not create duplicate findings.

2.09.40 — Analysis provenance

Every AI analysis must retain:

analysis_run_id
model provider
model identifier/version
prompt/configuration version
source document/version
retrieval identifiers if RAG was used
execution timestamp
output hash
validation status

You already created the AI run model in 1.19; reuse it.

Do not duplicate AI provenance inside every module.

2.09.41 — Important anti-hallucination rule

For every AI finding, enforce:

source exists
AND
source belongs to agreement
AND
source belongs to analyzed version
AND
source excerpt is verifiable
AND
output matches schema

Otherwise:

discard candidate

Not:

show low-confidence warning

A finding with unverifiable evidence should not enter the authoritative risk register.

2.09.43 — Resolution must require evidence

Do not permit:

POST /risk/findings/{id}/resolve

with just:

{
  "status": "resolved"
}

Instead, resolution requires one of:

verified remediation evidence
new amendment/version
verified compliance evidence
valid policy exception
authorized risk acceptance

Example:

async def resolve_finding(
    db,
    finding,
    actor,
    resolution,
):

    validate_resolution_authority(
        actor,
        finding,
    )

    evidence = await validate_resolution_evidence(
        db,
        finding,
        resolution,
    )

    finding.status = RiskStatus.RESOLVED

    await create_audit_event(
        db,
        actor_id=actor.id,
        action="RISK_FINDING_RESOLVED",
        entity_id=finding.id,
        metadata={
            "evidence_id": str(evidence.id)
        },
    )

    await db.commit()
2.09.44 — Escalation

Use the obligation notification infrastructure where possible.

Example rule:

{
  "condition": {
    "finding_status": "OPEN",
    "severity": "CRITICAL",
    "age_days": 2
  },
  "action": {
    "notify": [
      "actual-configured-role"
    ]
  }
}

The scheduler evaluates actual findings.

async def evaluate_risk_escalations(db):

    findings = await find_escalation_candidates(db)

    for finding in findings:

        recipients = (
            await resolve_finding_escalation_recipients(
                db,
                finding,
            )
        )

        for recipient in recipients:

            await create_idempotent_notification(
                db=db,
                recipient=recipient,
                notification_type="RISK_ESCALATION",
                entity_id=finding.id,
            )

async def test_ai_finding_requires_verifiable_evidence(
    invalid_ai_candidate,

async def test_unrelated_user_cannot_view_finding(
    finding,
    unrelated_user,
):

    response = await client.get(
        f"/api/v1/risk/findings/{finding.id}",
        headers=auth_header(unrelated_user),
    )

    assert response.status_code == 404
Old findings preserved
async def test_old_version_finding_is_preserved(
    finding_v5,
    version_v6,
):

    await analyze_new_version(
        agreement_id=finding_v5.agreement_id,
        version_id=version_v6.id,
    )

    old = await get_finding(
        finding_v5.id
    )

    assert old.version_id != version_v6.id
Resolution needs evidence
async def test_resolution_requires_evidence(

2.10 — Contract Intelligence & Advanced AI Workspace

This is the layer that makes Aariya genuinely useful when working with a large contract repository.

The architecture should be:

AUTHORITATIVE CONTRACT DATA
        │
        ├── Agreements
        ├── Clauses
        ├── Versions
        ├── Executed documents
        ├── Amendments
        ├── Obligations
        ├── Risk findings
        ├── Audit/evidence
        └── Organization policies
                ↓
        INTELLIGENCE PIPELINE
                │
        ┌───────┼────────┐
        ↓       ↓        ↓
      Search  Retrieval  Analysis
        │       │        │
        └───────┼────────┘
                ↓
          AI ORCHESTRATOR
                ↓
       SOURCE-VERIFIED ANSWER
                ↓
   exact citations + permissions

The fundamental rule remains:

Aariya may reason over contract data, but it must never silently become the source of truth.

2.10.3 — AI provider abstraction

Don't make the entire platform dependent on one LLM provider.

# backend/app/intelligence/providers/llm.py

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class LLMResponse:
    text: str
    model: str
    provider: str
    usage: dict
    metadata: dict


class LLMProvider(ABC):

    @abstractmethod
    async def generate(
        self,
        *,
        system_prompt: str,
        messages: list[dict],
        response_schema: dict | None = None,
    ) -> LLMResponse:
        raise NotImplementedError

Then actual providers implement this interface.

OpenAI-compatible provider
Other provider
Self-hosted model
Enterprise provider

The rest of Aariya doesn't care which one is being used.

2.10.4 — Embedding abstraction
# backend/app/intelligence/providers/embeddings.py

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class EmbeddingProvider(ABC):

    @abstractmethod
    async def embed(
        self,
        texts: list[str],
    ) -> list[list[float]]:
        raise NotImplementedError

This lets the storage/search layer work independently of the embedding model.

2.10.5 — Knowledge chunks

Do not embed whole PDFs as one giant vector.

Split them into meaningful legal units.

class KnowledgeChunk(Base):
    __tablename__ = "knowledge_chunks"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid.uuid4,
    )

    organization_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("organizations.id"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    agreement_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("agreements.id"),
        index=True,
    )

    document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("documents.id"),
    )

    version_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
    )

    clause_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("agreement_clauses.id"),
    )

    sequence_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        Integer,
        nullable=False,
    )

    heading: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(500),
    )

    content: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    token_count: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
        Integer,
        nullable=False,
    )

    metadata: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

Each chunk keeps its legal provenance.

2.10.6 — Embedding storage

For PostgreSQL, use a vector-capable extension such as pgvector.

Conceptually:

class KnowledgeEmbedding(Base):
    __tablename__ = "knowledge_embeddings"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid.uuid4,
    )

    chunk_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("knowledge_chunks.id"),
        nullable=False,
        unique=True,
    )

    embedding_model: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    model_version: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    content_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(64),
        nullable=False,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

The vector column itself is provider/model dependent and should be dimensioned from the actual embedding model configuration.

Don't hardcode a random dimension.

2.10.7 — Why content_hash matters

Suppose:

Clause text
   ↓
Embedding

Then the clause changes.

You should not continue using the old embedding.

new content
   ↓
new hash
   ↓
new embedding

That allows exact cache invalidation.

2.10.8 — Ingestion pipeline

When a contract becomes available:

Document
  ↓
Text extraction
  ↓
Clause segmentation
  ↓
Chunk creation
  ↓
Content hash
  ↓
Embedding
  ↓
Vector storage
  ↓
Search index

Use the existing document/extraction infrastructure from earlier milestones.

async def index_contract(
    db,
    agreement_id,
    version_id,
):

    version = await load_exact_version(
        db,
        agreement_id,
        version_id,
    )

    authorize_indexing_source(
        version
    )

    chunks = await build_legal_chunks(
        db,
        version,
    )

    for chunk in chunks:

        existing = await find_chunk_by_hash(
            db,
            chunk.content_hash,
        )

        if existing:
            continue

        embedding = await embedding_provider.embed(
            [chunk.content]
        )

        await persist_chunk_and_embedding(
            db,
            chunk,
            embedding[0],
        )
2.10.9 — Legal-aware chunking

Generic token splitting is not enough.

Prefer hierarchy:

Document
 ├── Article
 │    ├── Section
 │    │    ├── Clause
 │    │    └── Subclause

Preserve:

document
agreement
version
article
section
clause
page
sequence
heading

This gives better retrieval and better citations.

2.10.10 — Retrieval pipeline

The question:

“What is the termination notice period?”

should not immediately go to the LLM.

First:

Question
 ↓
Intent detection
 ↓
Permission filter
 ↓
Metadata filter
 ↓
Lexical search
 +
Semantic search
 ↓
Ranking
 ↓
Top evidence
 ↓
LLM synthesis
 ↓
Citation verification
2.10.11 — Permission-filtered retrieval

This is one of the most important components.

Never do:

SELECT * FROM knowledge_chunks
ORDER BY similarity

then ask the AI to hide what the user cannot see.

Instead:

query = (
    select(KnowledgeChunk)
    .where(
        KnowledgeChunk.organization_id == user_org_id
    )
    .where(
        authorized_chunk_filter(user)
    )
)

Authorization is applied before retrieval.

2.10.12 — Retrieval context
class RetrievalContext:
    user_id: UUID
    organization_id: UUID
    agreement_ids: list[UUID] | None
    allowed_document_ids: set[UUID]
    allowed_version_ids: set[UUID]

The retrieval engine receives this context.

async def retrieve(
    *,
    question: str,
    context: RetrievalContext,
    limit: int = 12,
):

    lexical = await lexical_search(
        question,
        context,
    )

    semantic = await semantic_search(
        question,
        context,
    )

    merged = merge_results(
        lexical,
        semantic,
    )

    ranked = rerank(
        question,
        merged,
    )

    return ranked[:limit]
2.10.13 — Hybrid retrieval

Use both:

Lexical
→ exact legal language

Semantic
→ conceptual similarity

Example:

The user asks:

"What happens if the customer ends the contract early?"

A lexical search might miss:

"termination for convenience"

Semantic retrieval can find it.

A legal search should combine both.

2.10.14 — Retrieval result
@dataclass
class RetrievedEvidence:
    chunk_id: UUID
    agreement_id: UUID
    document_id: UUID
    version_id: UUID
    clause_id: UUID | None
    content: str
    score: float
    source_metadata: dict

Do not pass raw database rows directly to the model.

Construct a controlled context representation.

2.10.15 — Context packing
def build_context(
    evidence: list[RetrievedEvidence],
) -> str:

    sections = []

    for index, item in enumerate(evidence, start=1):

        sections.append(
            f"""
SOURCE {index}

Agreement: {item.agreement_id}
Version: {item.version_id}
Document: {item.document_id}
Clause: {item.clause_id}

TEXT:
{item.content}
"""
        )

    return "\n".join(sections)

This makes citations deterministic.

2.10.16 — AI answer schema

Never accept arbitrary text as the final structured result.

class IntelligenceAnswer(BaseModel):
    answer: str

    citations: list["AnswerCitation"]

    uncertainty: str | None

    suggested_actions: list[str]

    requires_human_review: bool

Citation:

class AnswerCitation(BaseModel):
    source_number: int
    document_id: UUID
    version_id: UUID
    clause_id: UUID | None
    quote: str
2.10.17 — Citation verification

The model may return:

SOURCE 2

but the server must verify that source 2 actually existed in the retrieval context.

def verify_citations(
    answer: IntelligenceAnswer,
    evidence: list[RetrievedEvidence],
):

    evidence_map = {
        index + 1: item
        for index, item in enumerate(evidence)
    }

    for citation in answer.citations:

        source = evidence_map.get(
            citation.source_number
        )

        if not source:
            raise ValueError(
                "AI referenced unavailable source."
            )

        if citation.document_id != source.document_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "Citation document mismatch."
            )

        if citation.version_id != source.version_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "Citation version mismatch."
            )

        if not source_contains_excerpt(
            source.content,
            citation.quote,
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "Citation quote could not be verified."
            )

If verification fails:

do not return the answer as authoritative
2.10.18 — Intelligence orchestrator
class IntelligenceOrchestrator:

    async def answer(
        self,
        *,
        user,
        question,
        agreement_id=None,
    ):

        context = await build_retrieval_context(
            user=user,
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
        )

        intent = await classify_intent(
            question
        )

        evidence = await self.retrieve_for_intent(
            question=question,
            intent=intent,
            context=context,
        )

        if not evidence:
            return IntelligenceAnswer(
                answer=(
                    "I could not find sufficient "
                    "authorized contract evidence."
                ),
                citations=[],
                uncertainty="INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
                suggested_actions=[],
                requires_human_review=True,
            )

        prompt = build_grounded_prompt(
            question=question,
            intent=intent,
            evidence=evidence,
        )

        response = await llm_provider.generate(
            system_prompt=prompt.system,
            messages=prompt.messages,
            response_schema=IntelligenceAnswer.model_json_schema(),
        )

        answer = parse_structured_response(
            response
        )

        verify_citations(
            answer,
            evidence,
        )

        return answer
2.10.19 — No-answer policy

A strong contract AI must be comfortable saying:

"I don't have enough authorized evidence to answer that."

rather than hallucinating.

Use explicit states:

ANSWERED
PARTIALLY_ANSWERED
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
CONFLICTING_SOURCES
REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW
2.10.20 — Conflicting sources

Suppose:

Original agreement:
30 days

Amendment:
45 days

The AI must not simply retrieve both and randomly choose.

The intelligence system needs a temporal/effective-term layer.

async def resolve_effective_sources(
    db,
    agreement_id,
    as_of=None,
):

    return await consolidated_terms_service.resolve(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        as_of=as_of,
    )

Then the answer can say, based on the actual effective documents:

Current effective term: 45 days.

The original agreement stated 30 days, but an effective
amendment superseded that provision.

Each statement gets its own source.

2.10.24 — Comparison engine

Don't rely solely on an LLM.

Use:

Structured clause comparison
        +
Text diff
        +
Semantic comparison
        +
AI explanation
async def compare_contract_versions(
    db,
    left_version,
    right_version,
):

    structural = compare_clause_structure(
        left_version,
        right_version,
    )

    text_changes = calculate_redline_diff(
        left_version,
        right_version,
    )

    semantic_changes = await compare_semantics(
        left_version,
        right_version,
    )

    return build_comparison(
        structural=structural,
        text_changes=text_changes,
        semantic_changes=semantic_changes,
    )

2.10.27 — Precedent model

Do not create artificial “precedent” records.

A precedent is derived from actual contracts.

class PrecedentSearchRequest(BaseModel):
    question: str
    agreement_type_id: UUID | None = None
    jurisdiction: str | None = None
    limit: int = 10

Then:

async def find_precedents(
    db,
    request,
    user,
):

    context = await build_retrieval_context(
        user=user,
    )

    filters = build_precedent_filters(
        request
    )

    return await hybrid_search(
        query=request.question,
        context=context,
        filters=filters,
        limit=request.limit,
    )
2.10.28 — Privacy boundary for precedent retrieval

This must be strict.

A lawyer working on:

Agreement A

must not automatically see:

private notes
confidential unrelated agreements
documents outside their permissions
counterparty-private data

And organization-level precedent search must respect the document classification and membership rules.

2.10.29 — Negotiation intelligence

This connects directly to 2.04.

During negotiation, Aariya can analyze a proposed change:

Proposed clause
     ↓
Compare against:
     ├── current version
     ├── organization's approved policy
     ├── prior agreements
     ├── risk rules
     └── historical negotiation outcomes

Then show:

Potential impact

Liability → HIGHER EXPOSURE
Termination → NO MATERIAL CHANGE
Insurance → POSSIBLE GAP

Relevant previous agreements:
[authorized matches]

This is intelligence, not automatic negotiation.

2.10.30 — Negotiation suggestion schema
class NegotiationInsight(BaseModel):
    issue: str

    source_clause_id: UUID | None

    comparison_source_ids: list[UUID]

    impact: str

    risk_category: str | None

    explanation: str

    confidence: float

    requires_human_review: bool = True

The last field should be True for legal-negotiation recommendations unless your organization's governed workflow explicitly allows otherwise.

2.10.31 — Link intelligence to risk engine

Don't build separate AI risk logic.

Reuse 2.09:

Intelligence finding
       ↓
verified source
       ↓
ContractFinding
       ↓
Risk workflow

For example:

finding = await risk_service.create_ai_finding(
    agreement_id=agreement.id,
    version_id=version.id,
    source=insight.source_clause_id,
    category=insight.risk_category,
    ...
)
2.10.32 — Link intelligence to obligations

Likewise:

AI detects possible obligation
       ↓
source verification
       ↓
ObligationCandidate
       ↓
human confirmation
       ↓
Obligation

Never make AI answers and AI-extracted obligations two unrelated systems.

They should point into the same authoritative model.

2.10.33 — Contract summary

A summary should have levels:

Executive summary
Operational summary
Legal summary
Risk summary
Obligation summary
Lifecycle summary

Don't generate one giant generic summary.

Use structured data plus source-grounded generation.

async def generate_contract_summary(
    agreement,
    current_terms,
    risk_snapshot,
    obligations,
):

    context = build_summary_context(
        agreement=agreement,
        terms=current_terms,
        risks=risk_snapshot,
        obligations=obligations,
    )

    response = await llm_provider.generate(
        system_prompt=SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": context,
            }
        ],
        response_schema=SummarySchema.model_json_schema(),
    )

    return validate_summary(
        response
    )

2.10.37 — Conversation security

When reopening an old conversation, don't blindly trust the old citations.

At each new query:

re-authorize
 ↓
re-retrieve where needed
 ↓
verify current access

A user could lose agreement access after a conversation was created.

The system must not resurrect access through conversation history.

2.10.39 — Feedback must not directly retrain production

Do not do:

user clicks "wrong"
        ↓
production model changes

Instead:

Feedback
 ↓
evaluation dataset
 ↓
review
 ↓
benchmark
 ↓
candidate model/configuration
 ↓
offline evaluation
 ↓
approved deployment

This is much safer.

2.10.41 — AI evaluation metrics

Don't measure only “user liked it.”

Track:

Citation validity
Citation completeness
Source precision
Source recall
Answer groundedness
Unsupported assertion rate
Question refusal accuracy
Conflict detection accuracy
Structured-output validity
Latency
Token/cost efficiency

A particularly important metric:

unsupported_claim_rate

You want this as close to zero as possible.

2.10.42 — Evaluation pipeline
async def evaluate_intelligence_system(
    evaluation_examples,
):

    results = []

    for example in evaluation_examples:

        response = await run_intelligence_query(
            question=example.question,
        )

        score = evaluate_response(
            response=response,
            expected=example.expected_behavior,
            expected_sources=example.source_ids,
        )

        results.append(score)

    return aggregate_metrics(
        results
    )
2.10.43 — Model version registry

You already have model-run tracking, but intelligence should reference explicit configurations.

class IntelligenceConfiguration(Base):
    __tablename__ = "intelligence_configurations"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid.uuid4,
    )

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    llm_provider: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    llm_model: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    embedding_provider: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    embedding_model: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    retrieval_config: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
    )

    prompt_config: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
    )

    active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(

        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

Then every analysis references the exact configuration.

2.10.44 — Prompt versioning

Prompts are production configuration.

Don't bury them in random Python strings.

Use:

class IntelligencePromptVersion(Base):
    __tablename__ = "intelligence_prompt_versions"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(

        default=uuid.uuid4,

        String(100),
        nullable=False,

        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    output_schema: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(

Now an answer can be traced to:

model

source versions
2.10.45 — AI audit record

Each intelligence request should create a model-run record.

Reuse the model-run infrastructure from 1.19.

Record:

user
organization
conversation
question
retrieved source IDs
model/configuration
prompt version
output
citations
latency
token usage
validation result

Be careful with storing full prompts/responses when contracts are confidential. Retention and access policies must govern those records.

2.10.46 — Data minimization

Don't send the entire organization repository to the model.

The flow must be:

User question
 ↓
authorized scope
 ↓
minimal relevant evidence
 ↓
model

Not:

entire database
 ↓
LLM

This reduces:

privacy exposure
cost
latency
hallucination
irrelevant context
2.10.47 — Prompt construction

The system prompt should explicitly enforce grounding.

Conceptually:

GROUNDING_INSTRUCTION = """
Answer only from the supplied authorized sources.

Do not invent:
- contract terms
- dates
- parties
- obligations
- legal conclusions
- source references

Every material factual statement must be supported
by an available source.

If the evidence is insufficient or conflicting,
say so explicitly.

Do not treat an AI inference as an executed
contractual term.
"""

This is one defense, not the entire security mechanism.

The real protection is:

authorization
+
retrieval
+
structured output
+
citation validation
+
business-rule validation
+
human review

2.10.49 — Comparison endpoint
@router.post("/compare")
async def compare(
    payload: ComparisonRequest,
    current_user=Depends(get_current_user),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
):

    await require_version_access(
        db,
        payload.left_version_id,
        current_user,
    )

    await require_version_access(
        db,
        payload.right_version_id,
        current_user,
    )

    result = await comparison_service.compare(
        db,
        payload.left_version_id,
        payload.right_version_id,
    )

    return result

Never permit comparison to become an information-discovery mechanism for documents the user cannot access.

2.10.51 — Source panel

Every AI statement should be easy to investigate.

AI RESPONSE
────────────

"The customer may terminate for convenience
with 30 days' written notice."

Sources:
[1] Section 12.2
[2] Amendment 1

Clicking [Open source] should navigate directly to the document location.

2.10.52 — “Why?” explanation

For risk or obligation findings:

Why did Aariya flag this?

Detection:
RULE + AI

Evidence:
Section 14.3

Reason:
The configured policy requires X,
while the current clause states Y.

Related risk:
DATA_PROTECTION

Related obligation:
[actual obligation ID]

This is much more useful than:

AI says this is risky.
2.10.53 — Intelligence-to-action

AI may produce:

Finding
 ↓
Recommended action
 ↓
Existing workflow

Possible paths:

Create risk remediation

Create obligation review

Open amendment

Request lawyer review

Open source clause

Assign owner

Create compliance exception

But the action must always pass through the existing domain service.

For example:

await amendment_service.create_draft(
    actor=current_user,
    agreement_id=agreement.id,
)

rather than the AI itself modifying the agreement.

2.10.54 — Background analysis

Large contracts should not block HTTP requests.

Use:

Upload/execute/amend
      ↓
Outbox event
      ↓
Celery job
      ↓
Indexing
      ↓
Risk analysis
      ↓
Intelligence indexing
      ↓
Notification

Example:

@celery_app.task(
    autoretry_for=(Exception,),
    retry_backoff=True,
    max_retries=5,
)
def index_contract_task(
    agreement_id,
    version_id,
):

    async_run(
        intelligence_service.index_contract(
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            version_id=version_id,
        )
    )
2.10.55 — Re-indexing policy

Re-index when:

new version created
amendment becomes effective
document replaced
OCR corrected
embedding model changes
chunking strategy changes
search configuration changes

Keep old indexes where they are needed for historical analysis.

Do not make a historical version suddenly search as though it were the current one.

2.10.56 — Search index metadata

Every chunk should carry enough metadata to filter:

organization_id
agreement_id
document_id
version_id
clause_id
agreement_type
party_ids
effective_from
effective_to
jurisdiction
document_classification

This makes semantic retrieval substantially safer.

2.10.57 — Temporal retrieval

For questions such as:

“What did the agreement say before Amendment 2?”

the engine must use:

version timeline
+
effective dates

not simply retrieve the newest chunk.

Provide:

class RetrievalTimeScope(BaseModel):
    as_of: datetime | None = None
    version_id: UUID | None = None

Then:

if scope.version_id:
    filters.append(
        KnowledgeChunk.version_id
        == scope.version_id
    )

elif scope.as_of:
    filters.extend(
        build_effective_date_filters(
            scope.as_of
        )
    )

"Which contracts expire within the configured

"Show agreements with deviations from our

Every result must be permission-filtered before retrieval.

2.10.63 — Contradiction test
async def test_current_amendment_wins_over_old_term(
    agreement_with_amendment,
):

    answer = await intelligence.answer(
        user=authorized_user,
        question=(
            "What is the current termination notice?"
        ),
        agreement_id=agreement_with_amendment.id,
    )

    assert answer.status == "ANSWERED"

    assert cites_effective_amendment(
        answer
    )
2.10.64 — No hallucination test

A strong test is one where the evidence does not contain the requested answer.

async def test_system_does_not_invent_missing_term():

    answer = await intelligence.answer(
        user=authorized_user,
        question=(
            "What is the agreed minimum annual volume?"
        ),
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
    )

    assert answer.status in {
        "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
        "REQUIRES_HUMAN_REVIEW",
    }

This is more important than testing only successful answers.

2.10.65 — Privacy tests

Test:

lawyer A cannot retrieve party B private notes
user A cannot retrieve user B private conversations
organization A cannot search organization B
former member cannot retrieve old restricted contracts
revoked agreement access invalidates retrieval
legal hold documents remain accessible only to authorized users
2.10.66 — Performance

For production:

   ↓

   ↓

   ↓
reranking
   ↓
LLM

should avoid loading entire contracts into Python.

Use:

PostgreSQL

connection pooling

For very large organizations, the search layer can later move to:

OpenSearch / Elasticsearch-compatible search

while PostgreSQL remains authoritative.

2.11 — Workflow Automation & Contract Operations Orchestrator

This is a major architectural milestone.

Until now, the system has separate capabilities:

Agreement
Negotiation
Approvals
Signing
Repository
Obligations
Risk
Compliance
Intelligence
Lifecycle

Now they become one coordinated operating system:

REAL EVENT
   ↓
EVENT ROUTER
   ↓
RULE EVALUATION
   ↓
WORKFLOW SELECTION
   ↓
WORKFLOW INSTANCE
   ↓
TASKS / APPROVALS / ACTIONS
   ↓
WAIT / ESCALATE / BRANCH
   ↓
EXTERNAL SYSTEMS
   ↓
EVIDENCE
   ↓
NEXT STEP
   ↓
COMPLETION

The key rule is:

Workflows are configuration-driven. The application executes workflow definitions; it should not contain hundreds of agreement-specific if/else processes.

2.11.1 — What this milestone adds

The finished orchestration layer will support:

✓ Event-driven workflows
✓ Conditional branching
✓ Human tasks
✓ Approval tasks
✓ Lawyer review tasks
✓ Signature tasks
✓ Obligation tasks
✓ Risk remediation
✓ Timers
✓ Escalations
✓ Parallel execution
✓ Sequential execution

✓ Compensation/failure handling
✓ External API actions
✓ Webhooks
✓ Email/push/notification actions
✓ Workflow suspension/resume
✓ Workflow cancellation
✓ Workflow versioning
✓ Workflow audit trail
✓ Idempotency
✓ Dead-letter handling
✓ Tenant-specific workflows
✓ Organization policy workflows
✓ AI-assisted recommendations without autonomous legal mutation

2.11.3 — Workflow definition

You already have workflow concepts from 1.13.

Now make them capable of general orchestration.

# backend/app/workflows/models.py

from __future__ import annotations

import enum
import uuid

from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy import (
    Boolean,
    DateTime,
    Enum,
    ForeignKey,
    Integer,
    String,
    Text,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID, JSONB
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.database import Base


class WorkflowStatus(str, enum.Enum):
    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    DISABLED = "DISABLED"
    ARCHIVED = "ARCHIVED"


class WorkflowInstanceStatus(str, enum.Enum):
    RUNNING = "RUNNING"
    WAITING = "WAITING"
    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"
    FAILED = "FAILED"
    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
    SUSPENDED = "SUSPENDED"


class WorkflowStepType(str, enum.Enum):
    TASK = "TASK"
    APPROVAL = "APPROVAL"
    CONDITION = "CONDITION"
    DELAY = "DELAY"
    EVENT_WAIT = "EVENT_WAIT"
    ACTION = "ACTION"
    PARALLEL = "PARALLEL"
    SUBWORKFLOW = "SUBWORKFLOW"

2.11.5 — Workflow scope

A workflow may be:

GLOBAL
ORGANIZATION
AGREEMENT_TYPE
WORKFLOW_PURPOSE

Example:

Global:
standard agreement lifecycle

Organization:
Acme procurement approval

Agreement type:
SaaS vendor workflow

Do not hardcode which workflow applies to which agreement.

The resolver determines that from configuration.

2.11.8 — Workflow instance

A definition says what should happen.

An instance says what is actually happening.

class WorkflowStepInstance(Base):

2.11.11 — Generic domain event
class DomainEvent(BaseModel):
    event_id: UUID
    event_type: str

    organization_id: UUID

    aggregate_type: str
    aggregate_id: UUID

    occurred_at: datetime

    payload: dict

Do not put sensitive contract contents into the generic event payload.

Use IDs and references, then let an authorized worker retrieve the actual data.

2.11.12 — Event routing
async def handle_domain_event(
    db,
    event: DomainEvent,
):

    workflows = await resolve_matching_workflows(
        db,
        event,
    )

    for workflow in workflows:

        await start_or_continue_workflow(
            db=db,
            workflow=workflow,
            event=event,
        )

The workflow resolver determines:

organization
agreement type
event type
policy
workflow status

2.11.13 — Trigger definition

A trigger may look like:

{
  "event_type": "AGREEMENT_EXECUTED",
  "agreement_type_id": "actual-id"
}

Or:

{
  "event_type": "RISK_FINDING_CREATED",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "field": "severity",
      "operator": "IN",
      "value": [
        "HIGH",
        "CRITICAL"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

These are database configuration, not Python constants.

2.11.14 — Condition engine

Create a controlled evaluator.

def evaluate_condition(
    condition: dict,
    context: dict,
) -> bool:

    field = condition["field"]
    operator = condition["operator"]

    actual = resolve_path(
        context,
        field,
    )

    expected = condition.get("value")

    if operator == "EQUALS":
        return actual == expected

    if operator == "NOT_EQUALS":
        return actual != expected

    if operator == "IN":
        return actual in expected

    if operator == "NOT_IN":
        return actual not in expected

    if operator == "EXISTS":
        return actual is not None

    if operator == "MISSING":
        return actual is None

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported workflow operator: {operator}"
    )

Never evaluate arbitrary Python expressions supplied by a user.

Do not implement:

eval(user_expression)
2.11.15 — Compound conditions

Support:

AND
OR
NOT

Example:

{
  "operator": "AND",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "field": "risk.severity",
      "operator": "IN",
      "value": ["HIGH", "CRITICAL"]
    },
    {
      "field": "risk.status",
      "operator": "EQUALS",
      "value": "OPEN"
    }
  ]
}
2.11.16 — Workflow action registry

Actions should be registered in code, but selected through configuration.

class WorkflowAction(ABC):

    @abstractmethod
    async def execute(
        self,
        context: dict,
        configuration: dict,
    ) -> dict:
        raise NotImplementedError

Registry:

ACTION_REGISTRY = {
    "CREATE_TASK": CreateTaskAction(),
    "CREATE_APPROVAL": CreateApprovalAction(),
    "CREATE_OBLIGATION": CreateObligationAction(),
    "CREATE_NOTIFICATION": CreateNotificationAction(),
    "REQUEST_SIGNATURE": RequestSignatureAction(),
    "CREATE_AMENDMENT": CreateAmendmentAction(),
    "RUN_RISK_ANALYSIS": RunRiskAnalysisAction(),
    "CALL_INTEGRATION": CallIntegrationAction(),
    "WAIT_FOR_EVENT": WaitForEventAction(),
}

This is one of the places where code-backed functionality and database configuration properly meet.

2.11.17 — Action execution
async def execute_action(
    db,
    action_type: str,
    context: dict,
    configuration: dict,
):

    action = ACTION_REGISTRY.get(
        action_type
    )

    if not action:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown workflow action: {action_type}"
        )

    return await action.execute(
        context=context,
        configuration=configuration,
    )

Never permit arbitrary import paths from workflow configuration.

2.11.19 — Task assignment

Never configure a task as:

{
  "assignee": "john@example.com"
}

as a permanent hardcoded workflow dependency.

Use role/rule resolution:

{
  "assignee_rule": {
    "type": "AGREEMENT_ROLE",
    "role": "LEGAL_REVIEWER"
  }
}

Then the system resolves the actual member.

2.11.20 — Approval task

Reuse the approval subsystem.

Workflow
   ↓

   ↓
Existing approval engine
   ↓
Approval record
   ↓
workflow continues

Do not create a second approval database.

class CreateApprovalAction:

The workflow doesn't implement signing.

2.11.23 — Scheduler

The existing scheduler finds due timers.

@celery_app.task
def process_workflow_timers():

    async_run(
        workflow_engine.process_due_timers()
    )

Then:

async def process_due_timers():

    timers = await find_due_timers()

    for timer in timers:

        await continue_workflow(
            timer.workflow_step_instance_id
        )

Use row locking/idempotency to ensure only one worker advances a timer.

2.11.25 — Workflow engine

The engine needs a deterministic loop.

class WorkflowEngine:

    async def start(
        self,
        db,
        workflow_definition,
        context,
    ):

        instance = await create_instance(
            db,
            workflow_definition,
            context,
        )

        await self.advance(
            db,
            instance,
        )

        return instance

    async def advance(
        self,
        db,
        instance,
    ):

        while instance.status == WorkflowInstanceStatus.RUNNING:

            step = await get_next_step(
                db,
                instance,
            )

            if step is None:
                await complete_workflow(
                    db,
                    instance,
                )
                break

            result = await execute_step(
                db,
                instance,
                step,
            )

            if result.waiting:
                instance.status = (
                    WorkflowInstanceStatus.WAITING
                )
                break

Don't make this an unbounded synchronous loop across hundreds of steps. Persist progress after each meaningful transition.

2.11.26 — Step execution
async def execute_step(
    db,
    instance,
    step,
):

    step_instance = await ensure_step_instance(
        db,
        instance,
        step,
    )

    if step.step_type == WorkflowStepType.ACTION:
        return await execute_action_step(
            db,
            instance,
            step_instance,
            step,
        )

    if step.step_type == WorkflowStepType.TASK:
        return await create_task_step(
            db,
            instance,
            step_instance,
            step,
        )

    if step.step_type == WorkflowStepType.CONDITION:
        return await evaluate_condition_step(
            db,
            instance,
            step_instance,
            step,
        )

    if step.step_type == WorkflowStepType.DELAY:
        return await create_timer_step(
            db,
            instance,
            step_instance,
            step,
        )

    if step.step_type == WorkflowStepType.EVENT_WAIT:
        return await create_event_wait(
            db,
            instance,
            step_instance,
            step,
        )

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported step type {step.step_type}"
    )

        ┌── Legal review

2.11.28 — Parallel completion
async def all_dependencies_satisfied(
    db,
    step_instance,
):

    dependencies = await get_dependencies(
        db,
        step_instance.id,
    )

    for dependency in dependencies:

        source = await get_step_instance(
            db,
            dependency.source_step_instance_id,
        )

        if source.status != "COMPLETED":
            return False

    return True
2.11.29 — Real workflow example

A vendor SaaS agreement could be configured as:

Agreement created
        ↓
Legal review
        ↓
Security review
        ↓
Procurement approval
        ↓
Finance approval
        ↓
Party confirmation
        ↓
Signature
        ↓
Agreement executed
        ↓
Create obligations
        ↓
Create renewal monitoring

That is a configuration.

The engine doesn't contain:

if SaaS:
    ...
2.11.30 — More realistic branching

Suppose actual policy says:

Annual value below configured threshold
    → finance review

Annual value above threshold
    → finance + executive approval

Workflow:

              ┌── Finance
Start ────────┤
              │
              └── condition
                    │
            ┌───────┴────────┐
            ↓                ↓
        below threshold   above threshold
            ↓                ↓
        Legal            Legal + Executive
            └───────┬────────┘
                    ↓
                 Signing

The threshold comes from the organization's configuration.

Not from a Python literal.

2.11.31 — Retry handling

Actions can fail.

Example:

Workflow
   ↓
CRM API
   ↓
Timeout

Use retry policy.

class RetryPolicy:

    def __init__(
        self,
        max_attempts: int,
        backoff_seconds: int,
    ):
        self.max_attempts = max_attempts
        self.backoff_seconds = backoff_seconds

Store execution attempt.

class WorkflowActionAttempt(Base):
    __tablename__ = "workflow_action_attempts"

    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(
        UUID(as_uuid=True),

        nullable=False,

    request_metadata: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
    )

    response_metadata: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
    )

    error: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        Text,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

Never automatically retry irreversible legal actions without an action-specific policy.

2.11.32 — Idempotency

Every external action should have a stable idempotency key.

def workflow_idempotency_key(
    workflow_instance_id,
    step_instance_id,
):

    return (
        f"{workflow_instance_id}:"
        f"{step_instance_id}"
    )

This prevents:

workflow
 ↓
worker retries
 ↓
duplicate signature request

or:

duplicate CRM record

2.11.34 — Compensation

Not every workflow action can be rolled back.

For reversible external actions:

Create CRM record
      ↓
later workflow fails
      ↓
compensating action
      ↓
archive/remove external record

For irreversible actions:

Signing
Payment
Legal notice

do not pretend they can be rolled back.

Instead:

 ↓
incident
 ↓
remediation workflow
2.11.35 — Workflow suspension

Legal review may intentionally pause a workflow.

POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/suspend

Then:

RUNNING
   ↓
SUSPENDED

Resume:

POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/resume

Only authorized roles may perform these actions.

2.11.36 — Workflow cancellation

Cancellation should not blindly delete the workflow.

CANCELLED

with:

reason
time
affected steps
external actions

Existing legal records remain untouched.
